title: Design A Text Editor
description:
Design a simple text editor with a cursor. The cursor always sits between two characters (or at either end of the text), and it can never move outside the text.

Implement the `TextEditor` class:

- `TextEditor()` creates an editor holding empty text with the cursor at position 0.
- `void addText(string text)` inserts `text` at the cursor. The cursor ends up immediately to the right of the inserted text.
- `int deleteText(int k)` deletes up to `k` characters to the **left** of the cursor (like pressing backspace `k` times) and returns the number of characters actually removed.
- `string cursorLeft(int k)` moves the cursor left by up to `k` positions, stopping at the start of the text. It returns the last `min(10, len)` characters to the left of the cursor after the move, where `len` is the number of characters left of the cursor (an empty string if there are none).
- `string cursorRight(int k)` moves the cursor right by up to `k` positions, stopping at the end of the text, and returns the same 10-character window as `cursorLeft`.

Can you make every call run in `O(k)` time?

**Example 1:**
```
Input:
["TextEditor","addText","cursorLeft","deleteText","addText","cursorRight"]
[[],["helloworld"],[5],[2],["xy"],[10]]
Output: [null,null,"hello",2,null,"helxyworld"]
Explanation: Start empty. addText("helloworld") puts the cursor at the end. cursorLeft(5) moves it between "hello" and "world" and returns "hello". deleteText(2) removes "lo" and returns 2, leaving "hel|world". addText("xy") gives "helxy|world". cursorRight(10) can only move 5 steps to the end of the 10-character text and returns all 10 characters, "helxyworld".
```

**Example 2:**
```
Input:
["TextEditor","addText","deleteText","cursorLeft","addText","cursorRight","deleteText"]
[[],["abcdefghijklm"],[20],[3],["code"],[2],[1]]
Output: [null,null,13,"",null,"code",1]
Explanation: deleteText(20) can only remove the 13 existing characters and returns 13. cursorLeft(3) on empty text returns "". addText("code") gives "code|". cursorRight(2) cannot move and returns "code". deleteText(1) removes "e" and returns 1.
```

**Example 3:**
```
Input:
["TextEditor","addText","cursorLeft","addText","cursorLeft","cursorRight"]
[[],["abcdefghijklmn"],[2],["z"],[20],[3]]
Output: [null,null,"cdefghijkl",null,"","abc"]
Explanation: After "abcdefghijklmn" and cursorLeft(2) the 10 characters left of the cursor are "cdefghijkl". Inserting "z" yields "abcdefghijklz|mn". cursorLeft(20) stops at position 0 and returns "". cursorRight(3) moves to after "abc" and returns "abc".
```

examples.explanation: Start empty. addText("helloworld") puts the cursor at the end. cursorLeft(5) moves it between "hello" and "world" and returns "hello". deleteText(2) removes "lo" and returns 2, leaving "hel|world". addText("xy") gives "helxy|world". cursorRight(10) can only move 5 steps to the end of the 10-character text and returns all 10 characters, "helxyworld".

deleteText(20) can only remove the 13 existing characters and returns 13. cursorLeft(3) on empty text returns "". addText("code") gives "code|". cursorRight(2) cannot move and returns "code". deleteText(1) removes "e" and returns 1.

After "abcdefghijklmn" and cursorLeft(2) the 10 characters left of the cursor are "cdefghijkl". Inserting "z" yields "abcdefghijklz|mn". cursorLeft(20) stops at position 0 and returns "". cursorRight(3) moves to after "abc" and returns "abc".

constraints: text consists only of lowercase English letters
At most 2 * 10^4 calls in total are made to addText, deleteText, cursorLeft and cursorRight
solution_approach: The naive approach stores one string plus a cursor index and rebuilds the string on every insert or delete, costing O(n) per operation where n is the document length. The optimal design keeps two stacks (or dynamic arrays): left holds the characters before the cursor in order and right holds the characters after the cursor in reverse order. addText pushes each character onto left; deleteText pops min(k, len(left)) characters from left; cursorLeft moves min(k, len(left)) characters from left to right; cursorRight moves min(k, len(right)) from right to left. The returned string is simply the last min(10, len(left)) characters of left. Every operation runs in O(k) time, which is optimal since k characters may change, and total space is O(n).
hints: Everything happens at the cursor. What if you split the document into the part before the cursor and the part after it?
Store the text left of the cursor and the text right of the cursor as two stacks so that edits and moves only touch their tops.

Keep the right part reversed so its top is the character immediately after the cursor. Moving the cursor transfers characters between the stacks one at a time, and the report is the top 10 characters of the left stack in order.
follow_up_questions: How would you support undo and redo of addText and deleteText?
Could a gap buffer or a rope give better cache behaviour or support jumping the cursor to an arbitrary position?
